done.why: I had seen the house, forest, upper dungeon, dam and reservoir. What was left was the maze, the one-way chimney and chasing the thief, and I didn't want to do those.

about: A remixed Zork I. The house, trophy case, troll, dam and thief are the same, but the map is rearranged: the cellar leads to a gallery and studio, and the cave and mirror rooms connect oddly. You collect treasures and bring them home while a thief robs you.

moments.note: Down the trap door, the cellar's south exit led to a chasm and gallery, not the familiar layout.
The chimney only takes you plus the lamp plus one item, so I had to drop things.
The load limit blocked the trunk and the trident.
The maze gave no feedback, and the thief stole my painting and the bag of coins.
The thief's remark about the matchbook I dropped was a nice touch.
The grating can only be unlocked from below.
The egg in the tree was a pleasing find.

wished: A clearer way to tell maze rooms apart
To carry more, or a way to see what is heavy
To get back down into the dungeon after leaving by the chimney

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A new rule that forces a choice.

lines.line: The troll takes a fatal blow and slumps to the floor dead.
lines.why: The fight with the troll ends.

fun.why: Familiar ground with new twists, but I lost treasures to the thief and the maze was a slog.

engagement.why: The changed map kept me curious until the maze.

difficulty.why: Mostly fair. The weight limits and the maze were the friction.

interestingness.why: The rearranged map and the chimney rule feel fresh against the classic.

prose.why: Mostly the classic text, clean and terse.
